title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Scratch computation in the setting of graded modules over a divided-power algebra in one variable. The diagram τ_N S → τ_{N+ℓ}(S), labelled T^{(ℓ)}, together with the rule Σ T^{(i)} ↦ Σ c_{i,ℓ} T^{(i+ℓ)}, indicates that S = Γ(T) = ⊕_n Λ·T^{(n)}. Here T^{(i)}T^{(ℓ)} = c_{i,ℓ}T^{(i+ℓ)} with c_{i,ℓ} = binom(i+ℓ, i). S is viewed as a graded module over itself, so Hom^i(S,P) = Hom(S[-i],P) = P_i, and S is a free generator.

τ_N S = ⊕_{n≥N} Λ T^{(n)} is the N-th 'tail', a graded ideal. Multiplication by T^{(ℓ)} is a degree-ℓ map τ_N S → τ_{N+ℓ}S.

A module Q is 'négligeable' if each of its elements is killed by some τ_N, i.e. it is a torsion module for the topology defined by the ideals τ_N S. P ↦ lim τ_ω P is the associated localization or completion functor.

The chain of isomorphisms is Gabriel's formula for localization at the Serre subcategory of negligible modules: (L P)_i = Hom^i(S, LP) = lim→ over M' ⊂ S with S/M' negligible of Hom^i(M',P). Since the submodules τ_N S are cofinal among such M', this equals lim→_N Hom^i(τ_N S, P).

The right-hand box characterizes the essential image of the localization functor, i.e. the 'closed' or 'local' modules. P lies in it iff P → LP is an isomorphism. This holds iff Hom^i(S,P) → lim→_N Hom^i(τ_N S,P) is bijective for all i. The two conditions are:
(a) injectivity: P has no nonzero negligible elements (torsion-free);
(b) surjectivity: every homomorphism τ_N S → P extends to S, equivalently every extension of (S/τ_N S)[-i] by P splits (Ext^1(negligible, P) = 0).

This is the standard torsion-free plus 'divisible/closed' criterion of Gabriel localization. It presumably serves to identify the right category of graded Γ-modules (dual to modules over power series / completed objects) for the divided-power de Rham complex talk.
errors: Shift conventions are inconsistent from line to line: S[-i] versus τ_ω S[i], and S[i]/M' written where S[-i]/M' is meant.
The underbrace identification Hom^i(τ_N S, P) = Hom^i(τ_N S, τ_{N+i} P) depends on the degree convention for Hom^i, which is not fixed on the page. It is plausible but unchecked.
The cofinality of the τ_N S among submodules with negligible quotient is used tacitly. This is fine for finitely generated (cyclic) S, but it is not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Computing the localization of a module via a direct limit of Hom from 'dense' submodules (submodules with negligible quotient)
ideas.modern_name: Gabriel localization / quotient category by a Serre (localizing) subcategory; torsion theories
ideas.where_published: Related localization material appears in SGA4 Exp. II–III (sheafification as a filtered colimit), but not this specific graded computation.

ideas.what: Characterization of the essential image of the localization: no negligible elements, and Ext^1(negligible, P) = 0
ideas.modern_name: closed / torsion-free divisible objects (local objects) for a torsion theory

ideas.what: Divided-power algebra Γ(T), with the tail ideals τ_N and the multiplication T^{(i)}T^{(ℓ)} = binom(i+ℓ, i) T^{(i+ℓ)}, used as the generator S
ideas.modern_name: divided power polynomial algebra and its adic filtration

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine scratch verification of Gabriel-localization formulas in a graded divided-power setting. Nothing here goes beyond standard torsion-theory facts. The page is written on scrap paper; the next page is unrelated SGA7-style typescript on Néron models.
transcription_corrections: The left-hand side of the first line likely reads '(lim τ_ω P)_i', with the limit written in Grothendieck's shorthand. The completion/localization functor applied to P is the meaning in any case.
'S[i]/M' nég.' should be read as 'S[-i]/M' négligeable'.
In the triangle diagram, the crossed-out label is 'd°ℓ' (degree ℓ), and the target is τ_{N+ℓ}(S), not τ_N.
The final line reads 'toute ext. de [S/τ_N S][-i] par P est triviale', and the inserted word above 'homom' is '(chaîne)', i.e. a degree-preserving homomorphism.
